input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 2.1 imposes a multi-year (three-year) USD 2,000,000 per annum take-or-pay commitment on us expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — squarely the rule's walk-away position and well short of the fallback (single 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up rather than penalty). It also conflicts with § 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment), § 7.1 (no undisclosed minimum-use charge) and § 9.4 (Customer's 30-day convenience termination with refund of prepaid Fees), so the surrounding bargain is a no-minimum deal and the preferred position is proportionate. Redline replaces the take-or-pay with pay-for-what-is-used-or-ordered language, with the 12-month/true-up fallback offered in the comment.

proposal.summary: Remove three-year take-or-pay minimum and pay only for Services ordered or used
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay commitment: our playbook does not accept minimum purchase commitments, and a multi-year commitment with no reduction or termination right also conflicts with the no-minimum-volume acknowledgement in § 12.3 and the convenience right in § 9.4. If a commitment is commercially necessary, we can discuss one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice and settled by true-up rather than penalty.

ops.oldText: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: Customer has no minimum purchase commitment. Customer will pay only for Services used or ordered during the applicable term.
